diagnosis: A retained duplicate/inherited open file description keeps flock alive after the ledger owner closes its descriptor. The strengthened existing finalization/expiry replay test reproduces ResourcePersistenceInvalid deterministically before the fix. This establishes the lock-lifecycle defect; the original full-suite failure had no per-stage error instrumentation, so its connection to another concurrent fork remains an inference.
fix: Explicitly unlock the private file when the non-Clone ledger owner drops. It does not expose or transfer the private file. Competing opens still fail while the owner is live. Closing a stale duplicate after the replacement opens does not release that replacement owner's separate file-description lock.

verification.phase: retained duplicate regression, old production implementation

format: Only two changed Rust files formatted with rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true
limitations: No journal wire bytes, state transitions, charge release policy or authority changed.
No added retry, sleep, ignored tests or weakened replay assertions.
An abrupt death still relies on all inherited descriptions closing; this is not process-tree cleanup qualification.
Root owns aggregate full-suite rerun, frozen commit evidence and Git mutations.
